summary: Seven-stage partial design with 163 declarations. This continuation adds five specialized k-linear coordinate/Basis nodes, eleven API entries and nine distinct typed examples. Every inherited node ID/statement,78 routes,21 source findings,23 requests and29 planets is retained. The actual native basis/representation/degree portion of quadratic-pinch-generation now has signatures and a separate proof prototype. Generic basis and polynomial machinery is imported; complete bivariate presentation, normalization and global geometric/cohomological/model interfaces remain open. All statuses stay unchecked. This checkpoint supplies the complete native affine bivariate presentation:monic V-division,exact substitution range and kernel,and the canonical quotient algebra equivalence,including characteristic2 and repeated roots. Geometric and normalization/cohomology interfaces remain open.

nodes.title: Ferrand geometric pushouts
nodes.statement: For a commutative square Z→Y, Z→Z′, Y→P, Z′→P, a geometric pushout means the underlying space of P is the quotient pushout of |Y|←|Z|→|Z′| and the canonical sheaf map O_P→a_*O_Y ×_(ai)_*O_Z b_*O_Z′ is an isomorphism. A Ferrand datum requires i:Z→Y to be a closed immersion and g:Z→Z′ finite; a Ferrand pushout is its geometric pushout in schemes, or in algebraic spaces when the relevant existence theorem supplies that category. No scheme existence is built into the datum. Define the general geometric-square predicate first, then this finite-pinching specialization. For algebraic spaces the structure-sheaf equality is on the small étale site; the every-Zariski-open section formulation is its scheme specialization. Finite algebraic-space existence is supplied by G.0/algebraic-space-existence without the scheme affine-neighborhood assumption.
hypotheses: Schemes over a common base, or algebraic spaces over a common scheme base via the SF.1 carrier.
proofSteps: Use actual scheme morphisms and their maps on spaces and sections.

For every open U⊂P impose the pullback of the three section rings on a⁻¹U, b⁻¹U and (ai)⁻¹U; these natural conditions express the sheaf equality. In the algebraic-space extension use the small étale site and test the sheaf comparison on affine étale charts; Zariski sections alone are insufficient.
Restrict to closed i and finite g for Ferrand data; restrict instead to qcqs i and universal-homeomorphism g,a for Witaszek 2.17.

sources.match: Use the sheaf fiber product and quotient topology; global scheme existence is a separate theorem with affine-neighbourhood hypotheses.

proofSteps: Shrink V using finite closedness of g to remove the image of Z∖U.
Use the finite fiber algebra and a principal-open separation argument to obtain a section invertible on the entire fiber.

nodes.title: Conductor classification with one or two rational components
nodes.statement: Let C be a proper curve of canonical type over a field F whose irreducible components are birational to P¹_F. (r = 1) If C is integral with h⁰(O_C) = h¹(O_C) = 1, its normalization P¹_F → C fits into a cartesian and cocartesian square with a closed subscheme Spec R ⊂ P¹_F of length two, contracted to a rational point Spec F ⊂ C. R ≅ F × F gives I₁; R ≅ F[ε]/(ε²) gives II; R a separable (resp. purely inseparable) quadratic field gives Ĩ₁ (resp. ĨI). (r = 2) If C = C_1 + C_2 with C_i ≅ P¹_F, then P¹ ⊔ P¹ → C fits into a cartesian and cocartesian square over Spec(R × R) → Spec R with R of length two, giving I₂, III, Ĩ₂, ĨII correspondingly. Over a perfect field ĨI and ĨII do not occur.
proofSteps: Use the normalization exact sequence and arithmetic genus1 to force a conductor algebra of length2.
Apply the Ferrand conductor square and classify length2 algebras: split, dual numbers, separable quadratic and purely inseparable quadratic.
For two components use two identical copies of the conductor algebra and its diagonal map; over perfect fields eliminate the inseparable field case.

C has a unique relatively minimal regular proper model S→B. Its jacobian — the elliptic curve Pic⁰_{C/K}, or in the quasi-elliptic case the regular compactification of the twisted form Pic⁰_{C/K} of G_a — has a unique relatively minimal regular model with a section, the jacobian fibration J→B.
hypotheses: C is geometrically integral. For the DVR existence assertion assume excellence; the regular finite-type curve base is excellent. The regular nonsmooth case remains subject to the named quasielliptic source gap.
proofSteps: For smooth generic curves glue the imported unique local positive-genus minimal models along their common generic curve.
For a regular non-smooth generic genus-one curve, construct its regular compactification and relative minimal model with the quasielliptic Jacobian identified from its genuine Picard functor.
Extend the generic identity to the distinguished section by properness.

nodes.title: Picard constancy from resolved-surface point count
nodes.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically rational surface J/F_q with geometric Picard rank10, Pic_{J/F_q} is constant iff #J(F_q)=1+10q+q². In particular a rational Jacobian elliptic surface over F₂ has constant Picard scheme iff #J(F₂)=25.
proofSteps: Use rationality to identify H²_et(1) with Num(J)⊗Q_ℓ by the cycle-class isomorphism and H¹=H³=0.
Apply the geometric Frobenius trace formula to the smooth proper surface.

The Galois action on the finitely generated lattice factors through a finite group; all its eigenvalues are roots of unity. A trace of10 forces each to1, and finite-order semisimplicity makes the action identity.
Use the torsion-free étale Picard comparison to descend constancy from the lattice.

hypotheses: J/F₂ is a smooth projective geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹; the fiber lies over a rational base point, and all geometric Mordell–Weil sections descend to F₂.
proofSteps: The component met by O and the nonspinor terminal are fixed by distances in the weighted graph.
Suppose every section meets one of those two components. Shioda–Tate shows that the restriction image W→R* is R+Zω, where ω is the nonspinor terminal dual weight.
ω pairs integrally with that image because it pairs integrally with R and ω²=−1. Since W is unimodular, ω belongs to W.
This contradicts the evenness of W; a descending section therefore fixes one of the remaining terminals, and hence both.

nodes.title: Picard constancy criterion
nodes.statement: Let J be a smooth geometrically rational surface over F₂ with a relatively minimal jacobian elliptic fibration φ:J→P¹. Assume: (i) J_ā is irreducible for every closed non-rational a; (ii) no J_ā has Kodaira symbol I₀*; (iii) if J_ā is semistable, Γ(J_ā)→Γ(J_a) is a graph isomorphism; (iv) at most one rational b∈P¹ has J_b semistable or smooth supersingular; (v) MW(J/P¹)=MW(J̄/P̄¹); and Σ_{a∈P¹(F₂)} n_a=25. Then Pic_{J/F₂} is constant.
proofSteps: Use geometric Shioda–Tate generation by F,vertical components and sections.
Condition(v) fixes every section and condition(i) places reducible fibers over rational points.
Use condition(iii) and corrected additive graph rigidity to fix the component generators; the torsion-free étale Picard group then has trivial Galois action.
The stated point-sum assumption is retained; its relation to actual counts is the fiber-count-data node.

nodes.title: Large rational fiber
nodes.statement: Let J/F₂ be a smooth geometrically rational relatively minimal Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹ with constant Picard scheme and at most one rational base point whose fiber is semistable or smooth supersingular. Some rational fiber has at least six irreducible components.
proofSteps: If all component counts are≤5, absence of I₀* bounds every additive fiber by3 components and hence7points.
There is at most one multiplicative or supersingular smooth fiber; a split cycle of at most5 components contributes≤10, and a nonsplit small form contributes≤6.
The other two fibers contribute≤7 each, contradicting25≤10+7+7=24.

nodes.title: Model 1 certificate
nodes.statement: Over F₂, the relatively minimal resolution of the Weierstrass model y²+txy+t²y=x³+tx²+t⁴x+t⁵(1+t) has functional j=t⁴, discriminant t⁸ on the t-chart, and fibers at 0, 1,∞ of types I₁*+E₄+I₄.
proofSteps: Evaluate the baseline discriminant and c₄ formulas on this specific coefficient tuple; reduce the resulting rational j=c₄³/Δ.
Compute the weighted reverse chart. Factor the two discriminants to identify every rational and nonrational bad place.

At each bad place prove minimality, run the imported perfect-residue Tate algorithm, and transport its result to the actual regular resolution using the scheme-realization comparison; check splitting of the displayed residue polynomials.

Verify smoothness/rationality and relative minimality of that resolution, then sum the resolved fiber counts at0,1,∞. Use the geometric trace criterion to certify Picard constancy, without assuming Mordell–Weil descent from the printed list.

nodes.title: The two native conductor quotient charts
nodes.statement: Let f:Y→P be finite and schematically dominant, I=I_f, J=I.comap f, C=I.subscheme and D=J.subscheme. For every affine U⊂P set A=Γ(P,U), B=Γ(Y,f⁻¹U), f_U:A→B and K=c(im f_U,B). Then I(U)=f_U⁻¹K, J(f⁻¹U)=K, and the native quotient-chart identifications give Γ(C,C→P⁻¹U)≅A/I(U) and Γ(D,D→Y⁻¹f⁻¹U)≅B/K, compatibly with the actual inclusion and quotient maps.
proofSteps: I(U) is the chart ideal of conductor-ideal-sheaf. The common ideal K is contained in im f_U; consequently its inverse image extends back to K, by elementwise lifting.

nodes.title: Global geometric conductor reconstruction
nodes.statement: For a finite schematically dominant scheme morphism f:Y→P, the canonical square D_f→Y, D_f→C_f, Y→P, C_f→P is a geometric Ferrand pushout in Scheme. In particular its every-open structure-sheaf comparison is a pullback and its underlying space is the topological pushout. This derived generalization needs no Noetherian or reduced hypothesis; Witaszek’s finite-surjective reduced Noetherian case follows from native dominance. No birationality is required.
proofSteps: On an affine U⊂P, use conductor-affine-quotients and the already planned arbitrary-subring conductor reconstruction to identify A with B×_(B/K)(A/I).
Apply affine-existence to the quotient map B→B/K and finite map A/I→B/K. The latter is finite because it is a quotient of the finite A-module B.

The resulting geometric square is the restriction of the one canonical native conductor square, by conductor-induced-map. Thus the topological quotient identifications agree on overlapping affine opens.

The sheaf comparison agrees on a basis by localization, hence is an isomorphism of the actual structure sheaves and gives the ring pullback on every open. Glue this sheaf comparison and the local quotient topology; do not infer every-open section equality from global sections alone.
For Witaszek’s hypotheses, a finite surjective map is dominant and the reduced target makes it scheme-theoretically dominant by the pinned theorem.

nodes.title: Affine polynomial pinching algebra
nodes.statement: For a field k and q∈k[t], define A_q as the native k-subalgebra preimage of the constants in AdjoinRoot(q)=k[t]/(q). Thus f∈A_q iff there are c∈k and h∈k[t] with f=c+qh. The construction exists for every q; subsequent quadratic claims require q monic of degree2. It does not assert that q is separable or irreducible.
proofSteps: Take the preimage of the bottom subalgebra under AdjoinRoot.mkₐ. Algebra.mem_bot supplies an actual scalar witness; AdjoinRoot.mk_eq_mk identifies equality modulo q with divisibility by q. Rearranging the multiplicative witness proves mem_algebra for every q, including zero and units.
Use native Subalgebra, AdjoinRoot and the existing Ferrand ring pullback rather than introducing a new ring carrier.

The pinch_spanning API uses quadratic-normal-form-exists on h in f=c+qh, replacing its first coordinate by C(c)+tP. The added characteristic-two, inseparable and degree-one tests check these actual polynomial functions.

It is surjective and its kernel is the contraction of (q)⊂k[t]. The output is an actual AlgHom, not a freely chosen residue identification.

nodes.title: Two generators for a quadratic pinch
nodes.statement: For q=t²+at+b over any field, A_q=k[q,tq]. As a k-vector space it has basis 1,q^i (i≥1),tq^j (j≥1). These have degrees0,2i,2j+1 respectively, so no degree1 vector occurs.
proofSteps: Write f=c+qh by the native membership criterion and decompose h=P(q)+tQ(q) using quadratic-normal-form-exists.

In S=k[q,tq], native aeval into the subalgebra, aeval_subalgebra_coe and comp_eq_aeval show every P(q) and Q(q) belongs. Thus f=c+qP(q)+(tq)Q(q) lies in S. Conversely q and tq are in A_q, so adjoin_le proves S⊆A_q. This adjoin equality now has a native proof.

The native coordinates equivalence constructs the unique pair P,Q with f=P(q)+tqQ(q). Transport the product polynomial monomial bases through that equivalence; the resulting actual Basis has vectors q^n and tq^(n+1), and its Finsupp representation coordinates are the coefficients of P,Q.

The basis_degrees API proves degrees2n and2(n+1)+1; left n=0 gives1. Thus the advertised full vector-space basis and degree-family interface now have native signatures and a separately checked prototype. The adjoin equality remains its existing generation signature. A k[q]-module freeness interface, the bivariate presentation and geometric normalization are separate obligations.

nodes.title: Cohomology of the two-component pinch
nodes.statement: Let C pinch P¹_k⊔P¹_k along Spec(E×E)→Spec E, with the two chosen degree2 closed subschemes identified by specified E-isomorphisms. The incidence identification is part of the input, not equality of the residue fields by name.
proofSteps: Use the inherited global Ferrand existence: the two closed points lie in a disjoint union of affine neighborhoods, which is affine. Properness follows by the same finite-surjection argument.
The normalization quotient sheaf is j_*E, using (x,y)↦x−y from E⊕E modulo the specified diagonal E.
The global map k⊕k→E is (c₁,c₂)↦c₁−c₂; its kernel is the diagonal k and its cokernel is E/k. H¹ of each P¹ vanishes.
After splitting E, glue corresponding branches in the two components. Each geometric node has branches in different components; Frobenius exchanges the two edges and fixes the component vertices.

nodes.statement: For a separable quadratic E/k and a field extension K/k, both pinching constructions commute with K-base change via the existing flat-base-change theorem. The new conductor is E⊗_kK. When this is K×K, the one-component pinch is split I₁ and the two-component pinch is split I₂. Otherwise it remains a quadratic field. In the I₂ construction the components are already P¹_k; extending the field splits the nodes, not the component vertices.
proofSteps: Field extension is flat, so apply the existing four-arrow base-change comparison.
Use the imported separable quadratic tensor/Chinese-remainder comparison and track its two projections.
For I₁ the two normalization points are identified with one K-rational point. For I₂ each of the two conductor points glues one branch from each specified component.
Compare actual normalization and branch schemes with the imported graph carrier; record edge/half-edge actions without assuming trivial Galois action on all incidence data.

nodes.title: Point counts over every finite extension
nodes.statement: For the specified nonsplit I₁ and I₂ pinches over F_q, write Q=q^n with n≥1. Over F_(q^n), the I₁ count is Q+2 for odd n and Q for even n; the I₂ count is 2Q+2 for odd n and 2Q for even n. Counts of a nonreduced schematic fibre with this reduction are identical. These formulas apply to the fixed-component I₂ construction, and make no assertion for component-permuting forms.
proofSteps: E=F_(q²) has no F_(q^n)-points as an F_q-scheme for odd n, and two for even n. Import the standard finite-field embedding criterion.
For I₁ use the complement isomorphism: #(P¹\Spec E)+#Spec F_q. This is Q+1−0+1 or Q+1−2+1.
For I₂ remove the two copies of Spec E from P¹⊔P¹ and add one Spec E: 2(Q+1)−2e+e where e is0 or2.
A field-valued morphism kills nilpotents; import the reduction comparison. At n=1 recover the two inherited Schröer3.2 counts.

nodes.title: Uniqueness of quadratic polynomial normal forms
nodes.statement: For a field k and q∈k[t] with natDegree(q)=2, the actual function (P,Q)↦P(q)+tQ(q) from k[t]×k[t] to k[t] is injective.
proofSteps: First prove the zero-form criterion. If P(q)+tQ(q)=0 with Q≠0, P(q)=−tQ(q). Its two native natural degrees have opposite parity by quadratic-normal-form-degrees and natDegree_neg, a contradiction.
Hence Q=0. Polynomial.comp_eq_zero_iff gives P=0, because q cannot be constant.
Apply the zero criterion to the componentwise difference of two polynomial pairs, using the native composition/subtraction identities. Recover equality of both components and Prod.ext.

nodes.title: Linear coordinates in a quadratic pinch
nodes.statement: For any field k and a,b∈k, put q=t²+at+b and A_q={f∈k[t]:f mod q is scalar}, the existing native Subalgebra. Define the actual k-linear map M_(a,b):k[t]×k[t]→A_q by (P,Q)↦P(q)+tqQ(q). The product has its ordinary componentwise k-module structure. This is a linear map, not an algebra homomorphism.
proofSteps: The elements u=q and v=tq belong to A_q by its membership criterion, with witnesses (0,1) and (0,t). Use native aeval at u into A_q to define M(P,Q)=aeval_u(P)+v·aeval_u(Q). This construction proves membership without assuming the generation theorem or constructing a new carrier.

The two aeval maps are k-linear, and multiplication by fixed v is k-linear. Their sum on the product proves addition and scalar laws. aeval_subalgebra_coe and comp_eq_aeval give the exact ambient polynomial formula.
The monic displayed quadratic has native natural degree2 in every characteristic. The generic degree machinery is already in Mathlib; quadratic_natDegree is just this coefficient-specific helper.

nodes.title: Canonical linear equivalence for a quadratic pinch
nodes.statement: For every field k and a,b∈k, define e_(a,b):(k[t]×k[t])≃ₗ[k]A_(t²+at+b) as native LinearEquiv.ofBijective of the actual coordinateMap and its bijectivity proof. Its inverse assigns to f the unique polynomial pair (P,Q) with f=P(q)+tqQ(q). This is only a k-linear equivalence; componentwise pair multiplication is not transported unchanged.
proofSteps: Apply the existing LinearEquiv.ofBijective to M and the previous bijectivity theorem. No separately axiomatized inverse, new module structure or separability predicate is introduced.
ofBijective_apply gives the ambient formula e(P,Q)=P(q)+tqQ(q). Apply that formula to e⁻¹(f), then the native inverse law, to reconstruct f.
Native left and right inverse laws make the coordinates unique. For q=t², e(0,1)=t³, while e((0,1)²)=t³ differs from e(0,1)²=t⁶; the construction cannot be strengthened to a product AlgEquiv.

nodes.title: Native vector-space basis of a quadratic pinch
nodes.statement: For every field k and q=t²+at+b, construct an actual native Module.Basis (ℕ⊕ℕ) k A_q by mapping the product of the two native polynomial monomial bases through e_(a,b). The vectors are b(inl n)=q^n and b(inr n)=tq^(n+1). Thus the left index0 is1, the positive left indices have degrees2,4,…, and the right indices have degrees3,5,… . This is a basis of the existing subalgebra as a k-vector space, not a k[q]-module instance or a mere spanning-family assertion.
proofSteps: Use Polynomial.basisMonomials twice, the existing Module.Basis.prod to obtain a basis of k[t]×k[t] indexed by ℕ⊕ℕ, and Module.Basis.map along e to obtain a basis of A_q.
prod_apply, coe_basisMonomials and coordinates_coe evaluate the two summand vectors. The first is q^n; the second is tq·q^n=tq^(n+1). This treats left index0 explicitly.

The generic linearCombination_repr gives reconstruction by the native finitely supported coordinates. Infinite index sets require Finsupp.linearCombination, not a sum over a nonexistent finite enumeration.

natDegree_pow and natDegree_X_mul, using q≠0 and natDegree(q)=2, give degrees2n and2(n+1)+1. Every basis vector avoids natural degree1, but a basis vector can have nonzero coefficient of t, as q=t²+t+1 over F₂ demonstrates.

sourceIssues.printed: MW(J/P¹) = J(F) = Pic⁰_{Y_F/F}(F) = Pic⁰(Y_F), where F is the function field of the projective line. The latter equality holds because Br(F) = 0, by Tsen's Theorem.
sourceIssues.correction: Br(F) ≠ 0 for F = F₂(t). Instead: over F̄₂(t) Tsen's theorem holds, so L ↦ (L − (deg(L|Y_F̄)/2)R)|Y_F̄ is a surjective Galois-equivariant map Pic(Ȳ) → MW(J̄/P̄¹) for an F₂-rational two-section R. Since Pic(Ȳ) has trivial Galois action (constant Picard scheme), so does MW(J̄/P̄¹), and Galois-fixed sections descend: MW(J/P¹) = MW(J̄/P̄¹).
sourceIssues.reason: Tsen's theorem concerns k(t) with k algebraically closed. Br(F₂(t)) is non-zero: the cyclic algebra of F₄(t)/F₂(t) and t is non-split, since norms from F₄(t) have even valuation at t = 0. So Pic⁰_{Y_F/F}(F) = Pic⁰(Y_F) is not justified as printed. The statement (v) itself survives by the correction; /94 records it.

sourceIssues.printed: Theorem. (see Thm. 10.4 and Thm. 10.5) Up to isomorphisms, there are exactly eleven Weierstraß equations y²+a₁xy+… = x³+a₂x²+… with coefficients a_i ∈ F₂[t] that define a geometrically rational elliptic surface φ : J → P¹ with constant Picard scheme Pic_{J/F₂} having at most one rational point a ∈ P¹ where J_a is semistable or supersingular.
sourceIssues.correction: There are exactly fourteen such Weierstraß equations up to isomorphism: the eleven of Theorems 10.4 and 10.5 and the three recorded in the Theorem 10.4 issue. The paper shows only that every such surface is among its eleven, not that each has constant Picard scheme; the review's exhaustive search confirms that all fourteen do (for geometrically rational J, constant Picard scheme is equivalent to #J(F₂) = 25).
sourceIssues.reason: Theorems 10.4 and 10.5 say that under assumptions (i)–(ii) of §10 the fibration 'is given by exactly one of' the listed equations, and their proofs derive only necessary conditions. The converse would need Theorem 9.4, whose hypotheses include descent of every geometric Mordell–Weil section, and that is never checked. The TeX never cites Theorem 9.4 (\ref{constant pic}). The main theorem uses only the necessary direction, which /115 and /117 state correctly. Moreover the list itself is incomplete (Theorem 10.4 issue), so the count 'eleven' is wrong, not only unproved.

The additional models, with fibres over t=0, 1, ∞, are: y²+txy+t³y=x³+x² [I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, Δ=t¹⁰, j=t²]; y²+txy+t³y=x³+tx² [I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁, Δ=t¹¹, j=t]; y²+txy+t²y=x³+t²x² [IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂, Δ=t⁸(t²+t+1), j=t⁴/(t²+t+1), plus I₁ over t²+t+1=0]. Theorem 10.5 is correct. Proposition 11.1 (p. 33) and the key-reduction proposition of §11 take their elliptic column from Theorem 10.4. The proof of Theorem 15.1 reduces every fibration to I₁*+I₄ or I₂*+III+III. All of these must treat the three configurations; I₃* is never mentioned in §§11–15. On an Enriques surface Y, the multiple fibres would lie over the unstable and the E₄ points, because Ĩ₁ and Ĩ₂ are semistable. Until then the proof of the main theorem has a gap at this point. Whether the configurations occur on a non-exceptional Enriques surface over F₂ with constant Picard scheme is not settled here.
sourceIssues.reason: Checked by hand for y²+txy+t³y=x³+x². Δ=t¹⁰. At t=0 (Tate's algorithm): the reduction y²=x³+x² is singular at (0,0), and b₂=t², so the fibre is additive; v(a₆)=∞, v(b₈)=6, v(b₆)=6. The change y↦y+x gives a₂=t, a₄=t³ and P(T)=T³+T²=T²(T+1). Then a_{3,2}=a_{6,4}=0, and a_{2,1}X²+a_{4,3}X+a_{6,5}=X²+X has distinct rational roots. So I₂* with c=4, all seven components defined over F₂, 15 points. At ∞: y²+xy+y=x³+s²x², Δ′=s², node at (1,1) with tangent polynomial T²+T+1, so non-split I₂, 6 points. At t=1: y²+xy+y=x³+x² is smooth ordinary with 4 points (E₄). Total 25, so the trace of Frobenius on NS(J̄) is 10 and Pic_{J/F₂} is constant. Condition (ii) holds: only Ĩ₂ is semistable, and E₄ is ordinary. The other two models are checked the same way: I₃* at t=0 after three steps of the I_n* loop, and IV* at t=0 (Y²+Y distinct roots, c=3). Independent checks (scripts S/tate2.py, brute.py, classify.py, lcheck.py): (1) all 2²¹ equations were enumerated through their 2¹⁸ representatives with a₂=0 (every equation becomes one via x↦x+a₂), with Tate's algorithm at every place; this gives exactly 14 isomorphism classes, taken modulo the 512 coordinate changes of degree ≤(2,1,3) and PGL₂(F₂), that satisfy (i) and (ii); these are the 11 printed and the 3 above, one class per configuration; (2) for every class, the L-function of the generic fibre was computed from naive point counts at all places of degree ≤8; it equals (1−2T)^r with r=8−Σ(m_v−1), which confirms the component counts and the Galois-trivial Mordell–Weil action independently of Tate's algorithm; (3) for all 2¹⁸ normalised equations, Ogg's formula (v(Δ)≥e, δ=0 for I_n, IV, IV*) and Σ deg(v)·v(Δ)=12 hold. The proof's other claims were also reproduced: II*+E₂+E₄, I₃*+E₄+E₄ and IV*+E₄+I₃ are excluded, d₁=1 and 1+t are equivalent in the I₄* case, the second I₁* solution is twisted, and α=1 gives E₂. The error is the unexamined twisted case ('the argument is similar'): the tuples (r_a,i,r_c)=(7,2,2) and (8,2,1) yield these configurations.
